newsitem.title: UK: Copper tests $1,950 hurdle, contango evaporates.
newsitem.headline: Copper tests $1,950 hurdle, contango evaporates.

text.p: LME copper challenged the $1,950 barrier on Thursday afternoon as short term supplies tightened ahead of stock data that was expected to show another sizeable decline early on Friday.
The market got a fillip when the premium for three months metal over cash material disappeared for the first time since the market went into contango on September 17.
The cash/threes spread last traded even on the kerb after narrowing to a $3/5 contango on Wednesday from $9 on Tuesday.
The tightness was expected to make itself felt in LME inventory data on Friday.
One floor trader expected a draw of 12,000-15,000 tonnes compared to 8,825 tonnes on Tuesday, but another said that would be at the top end of expectations.
"We've heard stocks should decline by about 25,000 tonnes over the next week or two but we don't know how it will break down," he said.
Three months prices ended $22 higher at $1,944 a tonne after topping out at $1,949.
Speculative buying was behind most of the gains, traders said.
"It looks like they're gunning for those stops above $1,950. I think we'll see more of that over the next few days," one trader said.
Most of the rest of the metals followed copper higher.
Aluminium broke through nearby resistance at $1,410, finishing $16 higher at $1,416, but volumes were not huge, traders said.
Alloy was marked up with primary, finishing at $1,243/48, up from $1,225/30 on Wednesday.
Nickel surged through two layers of nearby resistance but eased back to end at $7,340, up $80 and $10 off its high. The next challenge would be to confront the $7,400 level, the high of September 20.
Tin confronted resistance at $6,100/10, but ended at $6,095, a $10 gain.
"Reports that Chinese exports are expected to be significantly lower this year should provide further encouragement to the currently depressed tin market," brokers Rudolf Wolff said in a commentary.
Lead and zinc only managed moderate gains, with lead closing $3 firmer at $782 and zinc ending $4 higher at $1,022.
